title: The GET /conservation-audit route is registered TWICE in repos/activity-api/src/routes/activities.ts with byte-identical
description:
The GET /conservation-audit route is registered TWICE in repos/activity-api/src/routes/activities.ts with byte-identical handler bodies (verified by diffing the two blocks: the only difference was a trailing brace from the slice boundary). The framework serves the FIRST registration, so the second is unreachable dead code.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.
1. Dead code: roughly 80 lines that can never execute.
2. BLOCKING: every anchor inside the handler now occurs twice, so any surgical edit to this endpoint hits an ambiguous old_string and cannot be applied. Adding a new invariant to this endpoint is impossible until the duplicate is removed.

HOW IT HAPPENED: two separate substrate-authored landings each appended the endpoint (ad41776 for gap route-edit-97c7b422, and 776456c for gap route-edit-c2ed2d92, which also added conservation-residual-trend). Both landed through the gated lane and both were verified only by the endpoint answering HTTP 200.

WHY VERIFICATION MISSED IT: a 200 response is served by the first registration and is therefore IDENTICAL whether the route is registered once or twice. An endpoint returning 200 does not prove there is exactly one of it. The check that would have caught this is a count of registrations for the same method+path, not a request against it.

FIX: remove the second registration of GET /conservation-audit (the later of the two identical blocks), leaving exactly one. Do not alter the surviving handler, and do not touch conservation-audit-emit or conservation-residual-trend, which are distinct routes and are correct.

NOTE: this gap has no literal-presence predicate because the defect is a COUNT (two registrations) rather than the presence or absence of a string, and the existing falsifier classes cannot express a count. The closing check is: exactly one occurrence of the route registration for GET /conservation-audit.
